text:
incident-bot: ALERT: continuous-batching path p99 latency breach in us-west-2 (streaming). Auto-page to #eng-oncall. p95 ~450ms, p99 ~3.2s, streaming stalls observed. Threshold exceeded for 3m.

lin: I'm on it — seeing the same on grafana: `cbatcher.stream.latency.p99 = 3.2s` spike at 12:08 UTC. No obvious infra maintenance. Any recent model rollouts?

deploy-bot: deploy: batcher-service@prod started rollback for commit `a8f3c9b` -> rolling back to `7b2e1fa` (triggered by oncall).

omar: grabbing logs from scheduler pods, will paste samples.

omar: ````
[2026-03-15T12:09:02Z] packer[batcher-3]: pack_shed evict batch_id=98765 reason=timeout size_tokens=12480
[2026-03-15T12:09:02Z] kvcache: miss key=user:kv:abc123, total_kv_mem=78%
[2026-03-15T12:09:03Z] scheduler: long_seq_alloc seq_len=6144 allocated_slots=8
[2026-03-15T12:09:04Z] streamer: stall detected stream_id=ff12 client_conn=keepalive
````

lin: looks like large sequences + pack shedding leading to KV eviction and streaming stalls. Mixed sequence length distribution has a heavy tail. That explains p99 jump while p95 unaffected.

priyanka: can we do a fast mitigation: temporarily cap max_batch_tokens and force pack-shed to prefer smaller packs? Proposed quick config changes: `max_batch_tokens: 768` and `pack_shed_prefer_small=true` on the live autoscaler.

samir: Also consider enabling `fair_preemption=true` so long sequences get preempted if they block many small requests. That should reduce tail.

lin: I can toggle the router-level long-seq rate limit and enable fallback-routing to dedicated pool `us-west-2-dedicated-2` for streaming traffic while we stabilize. Doing that now.

omar: rolling config to two scheduler replicas in us-west-2 to reduce queueing pressure (scaling).

lin: toggled `max_batch_tokens` -> `768` and `pack_shed_prefer_small` ON at 12:20 UTC. p99 dropped to ~1.1s at 12:28 UTC. p95 steady at ~420ms.

priyanka: good. Can we also add a temporary admission control rule to reject sequences > 8k tokens with a 429 and clear guidance to clients (we'll mark as fallback for 30min)?

lin: admission control added. I also opened incident DB-INC-2026-184 and added initial notes, affected customers list.

omar: customer reports: ACME (chat flows), NovaOps (streaming analytics), Ledgerly (document ingestion). All three reported stalls; two reported reconnects. Logged in incident ticket.

priyanka: drafting customer-facing status for status.redwood.ai — recommend "degraded streaming for large sequences; temporary mitigations applied; we are restoring normal latency." Will share draft.

samir: on longer-term fix: we need scheduler-level improvements: smarter bin-packing by seq_len, KV cache prioritization for hot prefixes, and an early preemption signal from runtime when pack queues exceed threshold. Adding to backlog with high priority.

lin: handoff to priyanka for next steps and customer comms. On-call handover: lin -> priyanka at 12:40 UTC. Remaining tasks: monitor p99 for 30m, validate no regressions on throughput, follow up with infra to replay KV evictions and ensure no cascading failures.

priyanka: taking over. I'll keep the temporary configs for 45 minutes then re-evaluate. I'll coordinate with infra to schedule a controlled rollback of config when stable.

deploy-bot: deploy: rollback to `7b2e1fa` completed at 12:33 UTC; batcher-service pod restart observed.

lin: confirmed new pods healthy. p99 now trending ~0.95s at 12:36 UTC. Streaming errors down to baseline.

priyanka: customer comms posted to incident DB and status page draft sent to SRE lead for review. Notifying account teams for the three impacted customers.

samir: filing a postmortem template item: root cause = mixed long sequences causing pack-shed + KV eviction under current batch sizing; mitigations = short-term config cap + preemption; long-term = scheduler fairness + KV hotkey protections + model quantization guidance.

lin: adding logs/graphs to the incident ticket. If p99 creeps back up I will re-alert.

priyanka: closing active paging for now, keeping thread open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
